news.title: Delhi police to replace all football players in a bid to win World Cup
news.lede: The Delhi police’s aggressive work tackling the protests against vote chori has earned them well-deserved rewards, not just promotions. To win the next World Cup, the Football Association of India has decided to replace all players with Delhi police personnel. The association took the unanimous decision despite all committee members voting against it. The House Minister, who also holds the additional charge of kicking, backed the decision he forced upon the association.

news.title: Scaloni extends Argentina contract until 2030 World Cup
news.lede: Lionel Scaloni has agreed to extend his contract as Argentina head coach until the 2030 World Cup, keeping him in charge of the national team beyond December 2026, when his previous deal was due to expire, according to Argentine journalist Cesar Luis Melo. The agreement ends speculation over Scaloni's future following an emotionally demanding period with the national team. His long-term commitment had been uncertain amid questions over whether he would take a break from the pressure of managing one of international football's most successful teams. Scaloni's future also came under scrutiny following Lionel Messi's retirement from international football, raising questions about Argentina's transition into a new era.

news.title: 'It's coming home': Meet the England players at the power football world cup
news.lede: Tomorrow is the final of the 2026 FIPFA Powerchair Football World Cup. After five days of footballing action England sit comfortably in first place, and will be headed to the final, if they can beat the US today. Also known as power football or wheelchair football, it sees two teams of four-a-side players compete using powerchairs with front bumpers. BBC Sport's Ellis Palmer went to meet the England players before the tournament kicked off.

news.title: FIFA: Azerbaijan is ready for World Cup
news.lede: Preparations for the FIFA U-15 World Cup and Festival, which will be hosted by Azerbaijan, have been completed, FIFA posted on its social media account, Apasport.az reports. In its post about the tournament to be held in Baku, football's governing body stated that the Hovsan Competition Complex had been made ready. "This complex was built by AFFA in just 66 days. Azerbaijan is ready for the FIFA U-15 World Cup and Festival," the post stated.
